note: Tier-0 entries only (assetName, id, pathType, plus the published attack path for review). Refresh with scripts/sync_azure_tiering.py; review every change before editing kb.js.

tier0.shortestPath: Can impersonate any agent identity with privileged application permissions granted for Microsoft Graph, which can be abused to become Global Admin.
tier0.example: TA identifies an agent identity (SP) with the UserAuthMethod-TAP.ReadWrite.All application permission (permissions such as RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory are blocked for agents). TA creates a new secret for the related agent identity blueprint, impersonates it and abuses the granted permission to escalate to Global Admin.

tier0.shortestPath: Same as Agent ID Administrator.
tier0.example: Same as Agent ID Administrator.

tier0.shortestPath: Can impersonate any SP with privileged application permissions granted for Microsoft Graph, which can be abused to become Global Admin.
tier0.example: TA identifies an SP with the RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory application permission. TA creates a new secret for the SP, impersonates it and abuses the granted permissions to escalate to Global Admin.

tier0.shortestPath: Can create a Temporary Access Pass (TAP) for a user who owns an SP with privileged application permissions granted to Microsoft Graph, sign in as the user with the TAP (which satisfies MFA), then impersonate the SP to become Global Admin. If the targeted user has Entra ID roles, it has to be roles for which an Authentication Administrator can perform sensitive actions (more info). The targeted user cannot be an owner or member of a role-assignable group, nor be in a restricted management administrative unit. Note: if TAP is not enabled for the user, the role can instead reset the user's password and register a controlled phone number as the second factor.
tier0.example: TA creates a TAP for a standard user who owns an SP with the granted RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory application permission (i.e. the user has no Entra role or role-assignable group assignment). TA signs in as the user with the TAP, satisfying MFA without knowing the password, adds a secret to the owned SP, authenticates as the SP and abuses the granted application permission to escalate to Global Admin.

tier0.shortestPath: Can impersonate a DevOps pipeline with assigned privileged Azure permissions, and leverage Azure resources to escalate to Global Admin.
tier0.example: A DevOps pipeline uses an SP with Contributor access to a subscription containing a resource with an assigned MI. The MI has privileged application permissions granted for Microsoft Graph. By triggering and impersonating the pipeline with Contributor access, the same path as Application Administrator can be followed. Note: many other paths of this kind are possible.

tier0.shortestPath: Same as Application Administrator.
tier0.example: Same as Application Administrator.

tier0.shortestPath: Can create a CAP blocking all users (including break-glass accounts) for all applications, apart from the compromised user account (making the tenant unavailable), and ask for a ransomware to remove the malicious CAP. Note: this role is Global-Admin-like, as it affects the availability of the tenant in the same way as a Global Admin.
tier0.example: TA creates a CAP blocking all users (including break-glass accounts) for all applications, apart from the compromised user account, and asks for a ransomware to remove the malicious CAP.

tier0.shortestPath: Can approve a GDAP relationship request from an attacker-controlled partner tenant that includes the Global Administrator role (or another Tier-0 role), granting Global Admin in the tenant to principals controlled by the attacker.
tier0.example: TA creates a GDAP relationship request including the Global Administrator role from a controlled partner tenant. TA approves the request in the customer tenant with the role, then uses a user from the partner security group mapped in the relationship to act as Global Admin in the customer tenant.

tier0.shortestPath: Can become member of a non-role-assignable group with assigned privileged Azure permissions, and leverage Azure resources to escalate to Global Admin. Note: can also acquire access to external solutions integrated with Entra ID via SSO, and providing access based on non-role-assignable group memberships.
tier0.example: TA adds the compromised user account to a group with Contributor access to a subscription containing a resource with an assigned MI. The MI has privileged application permissions granted for Microsoft Graph, and the same path as Application Administrator can be followed. Note: many other paths of this kind are possible.

tier0.shortestPath: Can add a federated domain to Entra ID and authenticate as an existing Global Admin without password or MFA requirements.
tier0.example: TA adds a federated domain to Entra ID, by importing a certificate with the domain's public key. TA generates a SAML token for an existing Global Admin with an MFA claim and signs it with the private key. TA successfully authenticates as Global Admin, without MFA requirements.

tier0.shortestPath: Can roll back service principals (including their MS Graph app role assignments), users, Conditional Access policies and the authentication methods policy to a state from the last 7 days. If a privileged MS Graph application permission was revoked from an attacker-controlled service principal (or a compromised Global Admin was disabled) within that window, can restore it and escalate to Global Admin.
tier0.example: TA's compromised service principal had 'RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory' revoked during incident response. TA triggers an Entra recovery job scoped to the MS Graph service principal, which restores the app role assignment, and uses the service principal to assign the Global Admin role to TA's account.

tier0.shortestPath: Can update the assignment policy of an access package provisionning access to Global Admin, so that requesting the package without approval is possible from the compromised user account. Has also the same path as Directory Writers.
tier0.example: TA identifies an access package providing access to a security group with an active Global Admin assignment. TA adds an assignment policy to the access package, so that the latter can be requested from the compromised user account, without manual approval. TA requests the access package and escalates to Global Admin via group membership.

tier0.shortestPath: Can run commands on a device belonging to a Global Admin and extract their tokens to impersonate them.  Has also the same path as Directory Writers.
tier0.example: TA runs a script on a device owned by a Global Administrator, extract their MS Graph tokens and escalates to Global Admin.

tier0.shortestPath: Can assign the Global Admin role to itself.
tier0.example: TA assigns the Global Admin role to the compromised user account (which already satisfies MFA), and authenticates as Global Admin. Note: many other paths are possible, such as the ones for Application Administrator and Domain Name Administrator.

tier0.shortestPath: Can create a Temporary Access Pass (TAP) for any user, including Global Admins and break-glass accounts, and authenticate with it to take over the account (a TAP satisfies MFA on its own).
tier0.example: TA creates a TAP for a break-glass account, authenticates with the TAP and escalates to Global Admin.

tier0.shortestPath: Can assign the Global Admin role to itself.
tier0.example: TA assigns the Global Admin role to the compromised user account, and authenticates as Global Admin.

tier0.shortestPath: Can invite an attacker-controlled tenant to govern the tenant and accept its governance request. The request's policy template grants Global Admin (via GDAP) to a security group in the attacker tenant.
tier0.example: TA sends a governance invitation from the compromised tenant to a tenant they control. From that tenant, TA sends back a governance request whose policy template maps the Global Administrator role to a group they control. TA accepts the request with the compromised user account, then signs in to the compromised tenant as Global Admin through cross-tenant delegated administration.

tier0.shortestPath: Can add the compromised user account to a non-role-assignable group with assigned privileged Azure permissions (or edit a dynamic membership rule or the account's attributes to match one), and leverage Azure resources to escalate to Global Admin. Note: can also update the assignment policy of an access package provisioning access to Global Admin (same as Identity Governance Administrator). Password resets alone do not lead to account takeover, as the role cannot manage authentication methods and MFA still applies.
tier0.example: TA adds the compromised user account (already signed in with MFA) to a non-role-assignable group with Contributor access to a subscription. TA refreshes its token to pick up the new membership, then runs code on a compute resource with an assigned MI granted RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory, and uses the MI to assign the Global Admin role to the compromised user account. Note: many other paths of this kind are possible.
